title: Faster arithmetic can still wait
hook: Double calculation capacity while input supply stays unchanged.

doesNotKnow: Recognize an unchanged data-supply limit after a compute upgrade.

misconception: Doubling arithmetic capacity doubles the complete system’s output.
objective: Recognize an unchanged data-supply limit after a compute upgrade.

claims.text: Computation depends on how components communicate and operate together.
John von Neumann, The Computer and the Brain (1958)
The original gives {A}; faster arithmetic still gives {B}. Input cannot supply work fast enough to use the extra calculation capacity.
Does it hold up? This ideal serial limit is exact inside the toy. It does not model a brain or machine parallelism.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}

recall.question: A scanner handles 3 items per step; processing rises from 9 to 18. What is serial output?
recall.why: The unchanged scanner still supplies only 3.
